title: The protocol state machine validates the message against the grammar but not against the session's authentication state
index_line: T-0028 · EXEC · a channel request is dispatched during the pre-auth phase; auth is a flag nobody consulted · erlang/c/python/ruby · corroborated
invariant_violated: A protocol implementation is assumed to reject a message that is not legal *for this session's state*, because it validates that the message is legal *for the protocol*. Those are different checks: a well-formed channel-open plus channel-request is syntactically valid at any time, and if the handler is dispatched on message type alone, 'not authenticated yet' is simply a state nobody consulted.

mechanism.does: the attacker completes the transport handshake and sends a channel request carrying a command, without submitting any credential
the server parses the message; it is well-formed and legal for the protocol at this point in the exchange
the connection handler dispatches on message type, and the authentication state is carried in a flag that this path never reads
the channel-request handler is reached in the pre-authentication phase — the session's authorization state exists but the dispatch never consults it
the request's payload is handed to the command executor, which runs it as the service account

source.protocol.value: any binary protocol with a pre-auth phase and per-session state (SSH userauth, MQTT CONNECT, AMQP open, an RPC handshake, a custom framing)

sink.exec.shell.value: the post-authentication handler that executes a command — reached from a pre-auth message

oracle.channel.value: the response to the request itself is the oracle: a well-formed reply (or command output) before any credential proves the dispatch happened

guard.session-state.value: the per-session authorization state; the bug is that the dispatcher selects the handler by message type and never consults it

preconditions.expr: the service exposes the protocol listener to the attacker

check.spec: ss -lntp | grep -E ':(22|2222|5672|1883)\b'; nc -w2 HOST PORT </dev/null && echo open

preconditions.expr: the implementation dispatches channel/session requests by message type before asserting the authenticated state

success: a reply to a channel-request arrives before any authentication exchange, or the requested command's side effect appears
the exchange works with no userauth packets at all — the attacker never sends a username
failure_like: the server closes the connection with a protocol error when a channel request arrives pre-auth
the handler checks an authentication flag before dispatch and refuses
false_positive: a transport-level reply (banner, key exchange) proving the listener is up — that is the handshake, not the bug
a connection reset interpreted as 'patched' when a proxy or rate-limiter caused it
testing only against the vendor's default config on a platform where the SSH app is not even started

hazards: this is a state-machine bug, so the audit unit is the (message type × session state) matrix, not the message parser; enumerate states and see which handlers are reachable from each
auth state is usually a boolean on a connection record; the bug appears wherever the dispatcher is written before the guard is added
protocol research pays here: the message that is legal-but-premature is the whole exploit, and fuzzers that only send malformed messages never find it
fixes add a guard at dispatch; any other path that bypasses the dispatcher (direct handler call, extension hook) re-opens the same hole
non_transfers: servers whose dispatcher is a table keyed by (state, message) — the illegal-in-this-state case has no entry
protocols with no pre-auth phase at all
